one.line: Jung on the One: the Monad of Monoïmos in Aion (CW9ii ¶340–341) and the number 1 in letter 63 to Pauli.

sections.title: The monad
sections.line: Aion (CW9ii ¶340–341, 1951): Hippolytus's report of the single Monad of Monoïmos, and Jung's comment on it.

quotes.text: This Man is a single Monad, uncompounded [and] indivisible, [yet] compounded [and] divisible; loving and at peace with all things [yet] warring with all things and at war with itself in all things; unlike and like [itself], as it were a musical harmony containing all things

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.voice: Monoïmos, in Hippolytus, quoted by Jung

quotes.text: This paradoxical idea of the Monad in Mono'imos describes the psychological nature of the self as conceived by a thinker of the second century under the influence of the Christian message.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

sections.title: In the letter to Pauli
sections.line: Letter 63 (October 1953): the number 1; the scan of the letter is damaged in this sentence and the quotation is kept as the scan reads it.

quotes.text: the One, absolute, nondivisible (advaita A two-less [Zweitlose]) and thus the unconscious, the beginning.

cite.workTitle: Atom and Archetype: The Pauli/Jung Letters

ql.name: State 00
ql.text: The indeterminate relating to the indeterminate. Pure potentiality, the psychoid shadow where forms remain asleep.

two.line: Jung on the two: the division of the One in letter 63 to Pauli, and the dyad and the self in Aion and Flying Saucers.

vonFranz.text: In this context, twoness signifies oscillation and rhythm, but not yet linear time.

cite.workTitle: Number and Time

vonFranz.text: The dualism of zero and one, or one and two, furthermore, contains within itself the potential concept of fourfoldness

cite.workTitle: Number and Time

sections.title: The dyad
sections.line: Aion (CW9ii ¶426, 1951): the self as a union of conscious and unconscious; Flying Saucers (CW10 ¶806, 1958): the complexio oppositorum of Cusanus beside the dyad.

quotes.text: Psychologically the self is a union of conscious (masculine) and unconscious (feminine). It stands for the psychic totality.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.text: The symbols of the self coincide with the God-images, as, for instance, the complexio oppositorum of Cusanus with the dyad, or the definition of God as a "circle whose centre is everywhere and the circumference nowhere" with Angelucci’s sign of the hydrogen atom.

cite.workTitle: Civilization in Transition

quotes.text: 2 = the division of the One, the pair, the connection, the difference

cite.workTitle: Atom and Archetype: The Pauli/Jung Letters

ql.name: State 01
ql.text: The indeterminate relating to the determinate. The emergence of form, the intrusion of the archetype into lived experience.

three.line: Jung on the three: the Trinity and the missing fourth (CW12 ¶25, CW11 ¶183, CW9ii ¶237), three as a relative totality (CW9ii ¶351), and the number 3 in letter 63 to Pauli.

vonFranz.text: According to this view the three then represents the unitary aspect of the bipolar one-continuum that has become conscious.

cite.workTitle: Number and Time

vonFranz.text: This is the reason why in number symbolism three is so often connected with time.

cite.workTitle: Number and Time

quotes.text: the dilemma of three and four

sections.title: Three as a relative totality
sections.line: Aion (CW9ii ¶351, 1951): three as a relative totality, and three where the context indicates that it refers to the self.

quotes.text: Three can be regarded as a relative totality, since it usually represents either a spiritual totality that is a product of thought, like the Trinity, or else an instinctual, chthonic one, like the triadic nature of the gods of the underworld—the "lower triad." Psychologically, however, three—if the context indicates that it refers to the self—should be understood as a defective quaternity or as a stepping-stone towards it.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

sections.title: In the letter to Pauli

quotes.text: the son, the first masculine number, etc.

cite.workTitle: Atom and Archetype: The Pauli/Jung Letters

ql.name: State 10
ql.text: The determinate relating to the indeterminate. The ego reaching back toward the unconscious, the act of symbol-making.

four.line: Jung on four: the mandala's arithmetical structure and the number 4 (CW10 ¶803–805), the quaternity as an organizing schema (CW9ii ¶381), and the whole judgment (CW11 ¶246).

vonFranz.text: The fact that mankind's repeated attempts to establish an orientation toward wholeness possess a quaternary structure appears to correspond to an archetypal psychic structural predisposition in man.

cite.workTitle: Number and Time

jung.text: They are as a rule quaternities (or their multiples).

cite.workTitle: The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche

sections.title: The archetype of order
sections.line: Flying Saucers (CW10 ¶805, 1958): the mandala as a symbol of the self, whole numbers as archetypes of order, and the number 4, the Pythagorean tetraktys, named in particular.

quotes.text: Psychologically, the rotundum or mandala is a symbol of the self.

cite.workTitle: Civilization in Transition

quotes.text: The self is the archetype of order par excellence. The structure of the mandala is arithmetical, for “whole” numbers are likewise archetypes of order. This is true particularly of the number 4, the Pythagorean tetraktys.

cite.workTitle: Civilization in Transition

sections.title: The viewfinder
sections.line: CW10 ¶803–804: the pattern of order compared to a viewfinder marked with a cross or a circle divided into four, and Jung's forty years of observing it in patients.

quotes.text: The archetype thereby constellated represents a pattern of order which, like a psychological “viewfinder” marked with a cross or a circle divided into four, is superimposed on the psychic chaos so that each content falls into place and the weltering confusion is held together by the protective circle.

cite.workTitle: Civilization in Transition

quotes.text: I have observed these phenomena in my patients for forty years and have come to the conclusion that this archetype is of central importance, or rather, that it gains in importance to the degree that the importance of the ego is lost.

cite.workTitle: Civilization in Transition

sections.title: The organizing schema
sections.line: Aion (CW9ii ¶381): the quaternity called an organizing schema par excellence, compared to the crossed threads in a telescope.

quotes.text: The quaternity is an organizing schema par excellence, something like the crossed threads in a telescope.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

sections.title: The whole judgment
sections.line: A Psychological Approach to the Dogma of the Trinity (CW11 ¶246): the quaternity and the whole judgment, and the natural minimal division of the circle.

quotes.text: The quaternity is an archetype of almost universal occurrence. It forms the logical basis for any whole judgment.

cite.workTitle: Psychology and Religion: West and East

quotes.text: The ideal of completeness is the circle or sphere, but its natural minimal division is a quaternity.

cite.workTitle: Psychology and Religion: West and East

ql.name: State 11
ql.text: The determinate relating to the determinate. Conscious rationality, the explicit mapping of known terms.

five.line: Jung on five: the quinta essentia and the quincunx (CW10 ¶738, ¶774), and how rarely the pentad occurs in his work with patients (CW10 ¶775).

vonFranz.text: It is included in the concept of the “philosophers’ stone” as the quinta essentia.

cite.workTitle: Number and Time

sections.title: The quinta essentia
sections.line: The quinta essentia in three passages: CW10 ¶738 (the circle divided into four with the centre), CW11 ¶160 (Johannes de Rupescissa's name for it) and CW8 ¶931 (Agrippa's spiritus mundi).

quotes.text: This is a symbol of the quinta essentia, which is identical with the Philosophers’ Stone. It is the circle divided into four with the centre, or the divinity extended in four directions, or the four functions of consciousness with their unitary substrate, the self.

cite.workTitle: Civilization in Transition

quotes.text: A famous alchemist, Johannes de Rupescissa (d. 1375),67 calls the quintessence “le ciel humain,” the human sky or heaven. For him it was a blue liquid and incorruptible like the sky.

cite.workTitle: Psychology and Religion: West and East

quotes.text: By the spiritus mundi, the ligamentum animae et corporis, the quinta essentia, which he shares with the alchemists, Agrippa probably means what we would call the unconscious.

cite.workTitle: The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche

sections.title: The quincunx
sections.line: Flying Saucers (CW10 ¶774–775, 1958): the four forming a frame for the one, and how often the quaternity and the pentad turn up in Jung's practice.

quotes.text: The fourth antithesis, unity and quaternity, appears united in the quincunx (Pls. III, IV), the four forming, as it were, a frame for the one, accentuated as the centre.

cite.workTitle: Civilization in Transition

quotes.text: In my work with patients the quaternity symbol crops up very frequently, the pentad very rarely, and rather less rarely the triad.

cite.workTitle: Civilization in Transition

ql.name: The Synthesis / 1
ql.text: The final return where the structure recognises itself. The quintessence that gathers the fourfold back into unity.

six.line: Jung on the hexad and the number 6 (CW10 ¶771, CW9i ¶679) and on the self (CW10 ¶805, CW12 ¶310); von Franz on six in Number and Time.

vonFranz.text: six is the first numeral of the series to represent the sum of its divisors (one, two, and three)

cite.workTitle: Number and Time

sections.title: The hexad
sections.line: CW10 ¶771 (Flying Saucers, 1958) and CW9i ¶679 (Concerning Mandala Symbolism): the hexad as a totality symbol, and the number 6 in old tradition.

quotes.text: The hexad is a totality symbol: 4 as the natural division of the circle, 2 as the vertical axis (zenith and nadir)—a spatial conception of totality.

cite.workTitle: Civilization in Transition

quotes.text: According to old tradition the number 6 means creation and evolution, since it is a coniunctio of 2 and 3 (even and odd = female and male).

cite.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious

sections.title: The Self
sections.line: Jung on the self as the archetype of order par excellence (CW10 ¶805), the archetype of wholeness (CW9i, 1955) and the centre and the circumference (CW12 ¶310); none of the three passages names six.

quotes.text: The self is the archetype of order par excellence. The structure of the mandala is arithmetical, for “whole” numbers are likewise archetypes of order. This is true particularly of the number 4, the Pythagorean tetraktys.

cite.workTitle: Civilization in Transition

quotes.text: Indeed, it could even be called the archetype of wholeness. Because of this significance, the "quaternity of the One" is the schema for all images of God, as depicted in the visions of Ezekiel, Daniel, and Enoch, and as the representation of Horus with his four sons also shows.

cite.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious

quotes.text: The self is by definition the centre and the circumference of the conscious and unconscious systems.

cite.workTitle: Psychology and Alchemy
